Diagnosis:
The test `testLargeSample()` fails due to issues when fitting polynomials using the PolynomialFitter on a large number of observed points (40,000 points). The current bug report states that new multivariate vector optimizers cannot efficiently handle large numbers of weights because a large n-by-n full matrix is created and copied when using n elements vector, which exhausts memory for large n. This matches the context of the test which fits polynomials with up to degree 9, meaning up to 10 weights, but with a very large sample size of 40,000 points.

The core of the failure seems related to the optimizer used by PolynomialFitter, which by default is the LevenbergMarquardtOptimizer instantiated in the test. The optimizer internally uses weight vectors and matrices to solve the least squares problem for the curve fitting. For large sample sizes, the current code attempts to allocate and handle a large full matrix in memory, which leads to high memory consumption or exhaustion, corresponding to performance and stability issues when fitting even relatively low degree polynomials with many observations.

Looking at the code snippet of PolynomialFitter.fit(double[] guess), it delegates to a fitting method on the parametric polynomial function but does not directly address or optimize handling for large number of points or weights. The memory issue likely originates in the optimizer implementation that PolynomialFitter calls.

Recent bug reports do not directly hint at a fix for large memory usage but mention related optimizer inconsistencies and bugs, which are somewhat related but not the primary cause here.

Hence, the test failure is due to the internal creation and copying of an n-by-n full matrix by the multivariate vector optimizer (LevenbergMarquardtOptimizer), which leads to memory exhaustion when fitting with a large number of points in the curve fitting process. PolynomialFitter currently does not provide a way to avoid this matrix handling issue on large samples.

The fix likely involves modifying the LevenbergMarquardtOptimizer or related matrix handling inside the curve fitting optimizers to better handle large sample sizes efficiently without full dense matrix copies.

Method to fix would be around PolynomialFitter.fit and LevenbergMarquardtOptimizer where the optimization and matrix operations occur.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
